descriptionChirho: The noun φθορά denoting the natural process of physical decay, decomposition, or the state of being perishable and transient. Used of the bondage to corruption from which creation will be freed (Rom 8:21), the contrast between sowing in corruption and being raised in incorruption (1 Cor 15:42, 15:50), and the escape from the corruption in the world (2 Pet 1:4, 2:19). Translations emphasize organic deterioration: Spanish 'corrupción,' Arabic 'فناء/فساد,' Hindi 'नाशवान में,' Korean '썩어지는 것,' Swahili 'kuharibika.' This sense covers the ontological condition of perishability inherent in the created material order.

The noun φθορά denoting active destruction, ruin, or moral degradation—a more volitional or judicial sense than passive physical decay. Used of false teachers who will be destroyed in their own corruption (2 Pet 2:12), the corruption of depraved conduct (2 Pet 2:19), and destructive moral ruin (Gal 6:8, Col 2:22). Translations reflect the destructive force: Spanish 'destrucción,' Hindi 'विनाश,' Swahili 'kuangamizwa' (to be annihilated), Arabic 'فسادهم' (their corruption). Korean '썩어짐' overlaps but contextually denotes active ruination rather than natural entropy.
